item.title: [IN PHOTOS] How Malta reacted to unexpected hailstorm
item.description: Although not impossible, such a sight in Malta is extremely rare, and so, when people in Rabat woke up to the unusual event, they made the best of it

item.title: Activists urge authorities to ensure access to Fort Tigne remains public
item.description: Flimkien għal Ambjent Aħjar called on the government to ensure that the fort remains in public ownership, ideally under a properly constituted heritage trust, and that public access is guaranteed

item.title: Trump slaps tariffs on European countries in attempt to bully them into giving up Greenland
item.description: US President Donald Trump says duties would increase to 25% on 1 June and remain in place until the US reaches an agreement to purchase Greenland

item.title: Robert Abela: No woman will go to prison for abortion on my watch
item.description: Prime Minister Robert Abela says he would use constitutional prerogative to recommend changing jail term imposed on women for abortion to non-custodial sentence

item.title: Prime minister opens up on election, housing, migration, planning reform and Greenland
item.description: In an unprecedented hour-long discussion inside the MaltaToday newsroom, Prime Minister Robert Abela addressed several issues raised by journalists. From the timing of the next election to housing affordability; from immigration to planning reform, and public projects like Manoel Island and Ta’ Qali, Abela engaged in a frank exchange

item.description: This speculation may make for interesting dinner or wedding conversations. It may provoke analytical news features that try to interpret and explain government decisions. But there is also the downside

item.title: WATCH | Gozo authority CEO Ivan Falzon: ‘I was, am, and will remain in favour of a permanent link’
item.description: Ivan Falzon, CEO of the Gozo Regional Development Authority, welcomes the Maltese people’s growing love for their sister island but warns that if not well-managed, economic growth can harm the island’s peace. He speaks to Matthew Farrugia about the opportunities and threats of change in Gozo
